title: burst-absorber: token-slot leasing for graceful microbatching under extreme QPS
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In sustained high QPS bursts we observe repeated GPU memory pressure events and p95 latency spikes despite existing batching and KV cache heuristics. Root cause analysis shows correlated arrival spikes create many tiny microbatches that bypass batch coalescing and stress per-request KV reservations; combined with KV cache fragmentation this leads to transient OOMs and request aborts.

Goal: Implement a low-latency 'burst-absorber' mechanism that leases token-slots to incoming requests for a short, bounded window to enable elastic microbatch coalescing while enforcing headroom for KV state. The feature must reduce OOM/abort rate during spikes, keep median latency impact minimal, and be safe to roll out incrementally.

Proposed design:
- Token-slot leasing: when a request arrives and immediate execution would create more than H token slots over reserved headroom, grant a short lease (T ms) that keeps the request in a local burst-absorber queue instead of immediate admission. Leases are short (10-60ms tunable) to favor coalescing without long tail latency.
- Elastic batch coalescing: leased requests are grouped into microbatches by sequence length and model-compatibility; coalescing occurs when either lease expires or coalesce-size threshold met.
- Soft KV headroom accounting: maintain a probabilistic per-GPU KV reservation estimate; admission checks compare worst-case required KV size + current reservations against a soft limit. On soft limit breach, new arrivals get leased rather than rejected.
- Priority-aware fairness: high-priority tokens (internal control plane, SLO-critical routes) bypass leasing or get smaller leases.
- Slot reclamation and preemption: if a node becomes critically memory-constrained, leases can be preemptively canceled and those requests retried or routed to fallback variants.
- Observability hooks: expose metrics slot_leases_granted, lease_wait_ms_p50/p95, queued_batches_coalesced, kv_predicted_headroom, lease_preemptions, and GPU_oom_aborts_by_hour.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Adds bounded extra tail latency for low-latency workloads; mitigated via priority exemptions and conservative defaults.
- Requires robust KV reservation estimator; estimator inaccuracies risk either unnecessary leasing (reduced throughput) or OOMs. We'll iterate estimator using production telemetry.
- Cross-node coordination not required for first iteration; later versions could use global admission signals for better load distribution.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reduce GPU OOM-induced request aborts during synthetic spike tests by >= 80% compared to baseline.
- p95 request latency under canonical spike workload increases by no more than 15% for standard priority routes, and no more than 5% for high-priority routes.
- Rollout gated by feature flag and canary to 5% of capacity with automated rollback on OOM regression or increase in error rate above 0.5%.

Implementation plan:
1) Simulation prototype (2 weeks): add simulator that models arrivals, KV size distributions, and token-slot usage; validate lease windows and coalescing thresholds.
2) Runtime prototype (3 weeks): implement local burst-absorber and token-slot leasing in serving runtime behind feature flag; add estimator and metrics.
3) Internal canary (1 week): enable at 5% traffic on non-critical clusters; monitor metrics and iterate.
4) Gradual rollout and tuning (2 weeks): expand to 25% then 100% with step-down rollback thresholds.

Monitoring & runbook:
- Dashboards: new 'burst-absorber' panel with the observability hooks above and KV cache fragmentation heatmap.
- Alerts: OOM_aborts_rate > 0.2% sustained 5m, or lease_wait_ms_p95 > 200ms triggers immediate rollback.
- Runbook steps: 1) disable feature flag; 2) increase KV eviction aggressiveness; 3) failover affected traffic to dedicated capacity pool if configured.

Links: design doc and experiment sheets attached below.
